newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Yunsa says to meet 1997 sales goal.
newsitem.headline: Turk Yunsa says to meet 1997 sales goal.

text.p: Turkish wool yarn producer Yunsa, Yunlu Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. will meet its $80-million turnover target in 1997, based on early results, a senior company official said.

"The results of the first five months of 1997 and the orders for rest of the year, show that we will meet our 13 trillion lira, or $80 million, total sale target this year," Yakup Gungor, general manager of the company, told Reuters.
"This result will lead to a two trillion lira pre-tax profit, with a 15 percent profit margin on sales," he added.
Yunsa reported 6.66 trillion lira turnover and 1.02 trillion lira ($7 million) pre-tax profit in 1996.
Shares of the company ended at 4,000 lira on Friday, steady from Thursday's close on the Istanbul Stock Exchange.

The company's 1997 sale target in dollar terms is equal to the 1996 results "because, we stopped our $11 to $12 million worth carpet production and expanded the wool yarn production by the same amount," Gungor said.
Yunsa is focusing on raising the share of exports in total sales. Its 1996 exports rose to $38 million from $30 million a year ago. The 1997 target is $43 to $44 million.

"Before the customs union between Turkey and the European Union began in January 1996, shares of the exports and domestic sales were 50-50," Gungor said. "But in the first year of the customs union, share of the exports in total sales rose to 70 percent and this year, it will be 80 percent."
He said they concentrated on overseas markets because imports soared domestically after tariffs were abolished as part of the customs union.
Main export markets include North America, Europe and far-east countries, with 50 percent going to North America. The other regions equally share the remaining 50 percent.
Yunsa spent $11 million last year on a new wool yarn line within the plant. The plant's production capacity increased by 20 percent to six million metres.
"We will spend $2.5 million this year for modernisation and overcoming bottlenecks in production lines, but a big step in investments will be taken next year," he said.
Yunsa plans to spend $13 to $14 million in 1998 for a new production line of wool yarn for women and to break ground for a new plant.
The company hopes the new line will produce two million metres annually, which would increase total capacity to eight million metres.
Gungor said the most important goal starting in 1998 will be construction of a new ready-to-wear plant.
"It does not mean that we will quit yarn production and become a ready-to-wear producer. We want to offer a ready-to-wear capacity to hundreds of producers who buy yarn from us," he said.
"We want to invest jointly with a company or a group who is experienced in the business," he added.
Yunsa reported 1.92 trillion lira turnover in the first quarter against 1.3 trillion lira a year ago, while net profit rose to 201 billion lira from 148 billion.
